newsitem.title: UK: UK electricity futures would be "helpful" - Offer.
newsitem.headline: UK electricity futures would be "helpful" - Offer.

text.p: British electricity industry regulator Stephen Littlechild said on Wednesday that the introduction of an electricity futures contract could be a "helpful" way of improving electricity trading arrangements and increasing market transparency.

He said that the current pool system guaranteed a market for companies to sell into and to buy from, even though they do not know the price, but added that "financial intermediaries" were not as ready to step into the UK market as they were in the US.
"I agree it would be helpful to move further and faster by the introduction of a futures market when it's possible to do so."
For the short term, he said, the pool was likely to remain in place at least until 2000, although he would not commit himself on how the market may change after that.

Littlechild believes the pool broadly reflects market fundamentals. He said it did not do so immediately after privatisation as prices gradually increased, but now prices have started to fall, reflecting lower prices of gas and coal and increased energy efficiency within the industry.
But in an industry where decisions to buy expensive plants involve planning 15 or 20 years ahead, he said "you don't expect prices to move from day to day."
